links.targetTitle: SkyLink rate limits use net accounting so round-trip flow do

title: SkyLink rate limits start low and are meant to rise as a bridge earns trust through operation
content:
A.4.2.2.2.3.2.2 sets the Solana SkyLink Bridge at 5,000,000 USDS per day and adds a policy statement rather than a value: "This limit should be gradually increased over time as the bridge becomes more mature."

That sentence is the claim. It treats new crosschain infrastructure as unproven regardless of how carefully it was reviewed, and makes the exposure ceiling a function of operating history. Bugs in bridges are notoriously found in production, not in review, so time-in-service with real value at risk is genuine evidence in a way that pre-deployment assurance is not.

It also converts a hard yes/no launch decision into a dial. Sky does not have to choose between withholding a bridge until certainty is reached and exposing the full balance sheet on day one; it can ship the bridge with a capped downside and widen the cap as the evidence accumulates. Combined with net accounting, the cap bounds worst-case daily loss from an undiscovered flaw.

The residual risk is that ratcheting up is a series of small, individually easy decisions with no natural stopping point, and the maturity judgment is qualitative. The safeguard is procedural: increases run through the Core Facilitator in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, so at least a designated risk role signs off on each widening.
description: The Atlas states the Solana limit "should be gradually increased over time as the bridge becomes more mature," making capacity a function of accumulated live evidence rather than audit sign-off.
